title: 25 Years After Dil Chahta Hai, Saif Ali Khan and Farhan Akhtar Are Reuniting — for a Thriller
excerpt: Excel Entertainment is pairing Sameer with the man who invented him for an untitled moral thriller that sounds like nothing either has done before
body:
In 2001, a first-time director with no film-school pedigree and an actor coming off a string of forgotten rom-coms walked into a recording studio with **Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy** and came out with a film that rewired an entire generation's idea of what Hindi cinema could sound and feel like. *Dil Chahta Hai* wasn't just a movie — it was a before-and-after line. Before it, Bollywood friendships were about sacrifice and tragedy. After it, they were about road trips to Goa and the quiet terror of watching someone you love fall apart.

Twenty-five years later, **Saif Ali Khan** and **Farhan Akhtar** are getting back together. And this time, they're not making a friendship film. They're making a thriller.

## The Project

According to a *Variety India* exclusive, Saif will headline an untitled film for Farhan and **Ritesh Sidhwani's** banner **Excel Entertainment**. The pitch is described as an "intense, edge-of-the-seat moral thriller" — a film that explores ethics, difficult life choices, and complex societal issues through psychological tension rather than car chases or gunfights.

The screenplay is in active development, with filming expected to begin before the end of 2026. A director has not yet been attached. Casting for a lead actress opposite Saif is underway.

It's early. The script is still being written. No one has announced a title. And yet — this is already one of the most interesting projects on any Bollywood slate this year, for one reason: the people involved have nothing left to prove, which means they might actually take a risk.

## Why This Pairing Matters

Farhan Akhtar didn't just direct Saif in *Dil Chahta Hai*. He unlocked a version of Saif that nobody had seen before. Before that film, Saif Ali Khan was a handsome footnote in multi-starrers — a guy who showed up, looked good, and was instantly forgettable. As Sameer, the serial romantic who couldn't stop falling in love with the wrong women, Saif found something he'd never been given space to find: comic timing that was effortless, warmth that was genuine, and a looseness on screen that made you forget he was acting.

> "It was insane. I think it was the most fun because it was Goa, and we were very young. We shot on the beach and we partied as well. I tried almost every restaurant in Goa." — Saif Ali Khan, in a recent *Variety India* interview

That Goa schedule has become its own mythology — the late nights, the discipline of Zoya Akhtar as an assistant director (estimated a 105-day shoot from the script and wrapped on day 105), the beach clean-up after the last shot. Saif has described the experience as the moment he understood what a well-made film felt like.

The question now is whether a "moral thriller" can channel that same instinct for surprise. Saif has spent the last few years building a fascinating parallel career — *Sacred Games* recast him as a serious dramatic actor, *Vikram Vedha* proved he could hold the screen against anyone, and more recently, Netflix India's *Kartavya* earned him quiet praise as a police officer navigating institutional rot.

He's also booked for **Priyadarshan's** *Haiwaan* alongside Akshay Kumar (releasing September 11, 2026) and **Rahul Dholakia's** Netflix historical about India's first general election. The man has range — and an Excel Entertainment thriller could be the project that lets him use all of it at once.

## Excel's Loaded Slate

The Saif project isn't the only *Dil Chahta Hai* reunion Excel is engineering. The production house is also bringing back **Aamir Khan** for **Ashutosh Gowariker's** upcoming sports drama based on the **1952 India–Pakistan Test Series** — a film that reportedly has Farhan playing a pivotal on-screen role as well. Production is set to begin in October 2026.

For a banner that built its reputation on *DCH*, *Rock On!!*, *Don*, *Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara*, and *Gully Boy*, Excel has always understood something most Bollywood producers don't: that stars are more interesting when they're uncomfortable. A moral thriller with Saif — no action set-pieces, no franchise safety net, just a man confronting difficult truths — sounds exactly like the kind of film Excel makes when it's at its best.

## What Diaspora Audiences Should Watch For

For NRI audiences who grew up on *Dil Chahta Hai* — who watched the DVD in their college dorm rooms, who used "Tum mujhe tang karne lage ho" as an inside joke, who planned their first Goa trip because three fictional friends made it look like the most important place on earth — this reunion carries a specific emotional weight.

It's not nostalgia. It's recognition. The people who changed how you thought about Hindi films are back, a quarter-century older and presumably a quarter-century sharper, making something designed to challenge rather than comfort. No release window has been announced. No title exists. But the reunion alone makes this one worth tracking.

Twenty-five years ago, Farhan Akhtar looked at Saif Ali Khan and saw Sameer — warm, reckless, a little foolish, completely loveable. Whatever he sees in him now, it's going to be a lot darker. And that might be exactly the point.
